verdict.rationale: Open WebUI documents a memory feature where users can add, edit, or delete memories under Settings > Personalization > Memory, and the platform is self-hosted and built to run entirely offline, which implies the memory store sits on the user's own infrastructure. Nothing in the evidence says how memories are stored or whether the format is open or exportable. missing for 10: documentation of where and in what open format memories are stored on disk, a memory export path, independent or hands-on corroboration of memory inspection and editing.

support.subject: As a privacy-first user, I can inspect, edit, and delete what the assistant has remembered — the memory store lives on my machine in an open format

citations.quote: Users can manually add, edit, or delete memories by navigating to: Settings > Personalization > Memory
Open WebUI includes a sophisticated memory system that allows models to remember facts, preferences, and context across different conversations.
self-hosted AI platform that's extensible, feature-rich, user-friendly, and built to run entirely offline
